sections.title: Judgment on Assyria
observations: In this section, God pronounces judgment on Assyria, which He uses as an instrument of His wrath against Israel. However, Assyria's pride and arrogance lead them to believe that their power is their own, rather than recognizing it as a tool in God's hands.

The imagery of the axe and the saw illustrates how God can use nations to accomplish His purposes, but He will not allow them to boast in their own strength. This serves as a reminder that all authority and power ultimately belong to God.

sections.title: The Remnant of Israel
observations: God promises that a remnant of Israel will return, highlighting His faithfulness to His covenant people. Despite the judgment that is coming, there is hope for restoration.
This section emphasizes the theme of grace amidst judgment, showing that God preserves a faithful remnant even in times of great distress.

sections.title: The Sovereignty of God
observations: The chapter concludes with a powerful affirmation of God's sovereignty over all nations. Even though Assyria is used as an instrument of judgment, they will also face God's judgment for their own sins.
This section encourages believers to trust in God's ultimate plan and purpose, knowing that He is in control of history and will bring about justice in His time.

importantVerses.commentary: Woe to those who decree iniquitous decrees, and the writers who keep writing oppression! This verse highlights the injustice and corruption in leadership, reminding us of the importance of righteous governance.

In that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no more lean on him who struck them, but will lean on the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. This verse emphasizes the shift from reliance on human powers to complete trust in God.

questions: What does this chapter teach us about the nature of God's judgment and mercy?
How can we apply the concept of a remnant in our understanding of the church today?
In what ways do we see the pride of nations today, and how should we respond as believers?
